newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees no major recovery in 1996/97 flour trade.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees no major recovery in 1996/97 flour trade.

text.p: World trade in wheat flour will see increased competition this season as prices fall, but no significant recovery should be expected in imports, the International Grains Council (IGC) said on Thursday.

In its latest monthly report, the Council estimated wheat flour trade at 8.3 million tonnes for 1995/96, down 1.4 million from the year before mainly because of sharp price increases and the absence of export subsidies.
Lower prices could fuel demand this year, but not to a great extent, the IGC said.

Russia, for example, which imported 550,000 tonnes in 1995/96 from non-CIS countries compared with 28,000 in the previous year, could further increase purchases because of reduced availability in eastern Europe and the Ukraine, its traditional suppliers.

"However, much will depend on the relationship between wheat and flour prices within Russia," the IGC said, adding that high domestic flour prices were mainly responsible for last year's upturn in imports.
Algeria has made some significant purchases since July and could continue to import, it said.
But export certificates from the EU, the world's largest exporter of wheat flour, amounted to some 1.5 million tonnes wheat equivalent to date, well below 1.9 million in the same period last year.
The EU sold a total 4.5 million tonnes of wheat flour in 1995/96.
